item.title: Number of days since Joey Barton’s last violent assault reverts back to zero
item.description: The number of days since Joey Barton last violently attacked someone has reverted back to zero…. again.

item.title: ‘Strait of Hormuz’ to be renamed ‘Strait of America’
item.description: The United States government have announced that the ‘Strait of Hormuz’ is to be renamed the ‘Strait of America’.

item.title: Spurs target swift Champions League exit to focus on relegation
item.description: Tottenham have targeted an early Champions League exit in order to focus on relegation from the Premier League.

item.title: Country whose problems all come from the House of Commons, reforms the House of Lords
item.description: The UK, a country reeling from financial and social problems caused by bad decisions in the House of Commons, is pleased to hear that hereditary peers can no longer be irrelevant in the House next door.

item.title: North Korean media reports Kim Jong-un rode Shergar to victory at Cheltenham festival
item.description: North Korean media is reporting that their dear leader, Kim Jong Un, rode the missing, inevitably long-dead racehorse Shergar to victory in the 1:30 at Cheltenham today.

item.title: ‘I didn’t realise what a bad guy he was,’ said Jeffrey Epstein on meeting Tony Blair
item.description: Notorious paedophile and sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein has apologised for his ill-judgement, admitting he would never have met with Tony Blair if he’d realised what a bad guy he was.

item.title: ‘Can I also have £75,000 for getting sacked and possibly breaking the law?’ asks rest of population
item.description: The UK population has today asked if they would be entitled to a £75,000 government payout after being sacked for possibly breaking the law.

item.title: Trump gifts staffers dress shoes with extra room for bone spurs
item.description: US President Donald Trump has gifted White House staffers and cabinet members dress shoes with extra room for bone spurs, it has been revealed.

item.title: ‘We don’t protect our own schools from guns, so why would we protect foreign schools from missiles?’ explains US
item.description: US Defence officials have defended the possibly accidental bombing of a school in Iran after senior figures argued it would be “inconsistent” for the United States to suddenly start worrying about children’s safety while they are in school.
